passages.original: Foris ergo peccata parebant, imus autem mysteria latitabant. Quæ ideo de nuru Judæ malui præterire, ne hoc opus multo ampliore longius sermone distendam. De unius denique facto, id est Loth uxorisque ejus (Gen. XIX), quid B. Augustinus contra Fanstum Manichæum perorans dixerit, pro generali similium intellectu locorum, huic operi conserendum putavi. Dicit enim : Sicut autem aliud genus hominum in ejus uxore figuratum est, eorum scilicet qui per gratiam Da i vocati, retro respiciunt, non sicut Paulus, qui ea quae retro sunt obliviscitur, et in ea quæ ante sunt extenditur (Philip. III). Unde et ipse Dominus : Nemo, inquit, imponens manum super aratrum, et respiciens retro, aptus est regno coelorum (Luc.
passages.english: Outwardly, then, sins were apparent, but in the depths mysteries lay hidden. I have preferred to pass over these matters concerning Judah's daughter-in-law, so as not to stretch this work out further with a much longer discourse. Finally, concerning the deed of one [man], that is, of Lot and his wife (Gen. 19), I have thought it right to insert into this work what blessed Augustine said when arguing against Faustus the Manichaean, for the general understanding of similar passages. For he says: "Just as another kind of people was prefigured in his wife, namely those who, called through the grace of God, look back, not like Paul, who forgets the things that are behind and stretches forward to the things that are ahead (Phil. 3). passages.original: In actu vero etiam publice coram hominibus adimpletur, quando opportunitas perseculionis innascitur. Aliquando enim videtur martyrium deesse animo, aliquando in aliis animum deesse martyrio. Hinc beatus Cyprianus dicit : Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum, Dominum confiteri : secundus ad gloriam gradus est, cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judicc, conscientia pura cordis integritatem conservat. Quod etiam de duobus filiis Zebedæi manifestissime comprobatur, quod Jacobus ab Herode necatus, publica confessione martyrio do.
passages.english: But [martyrdom] in act is fulfilled publicly before people, when an occasion of persecution arises. For sometimes martyrdom seems to be lacking to the will, sometimes in others the will seems to be lacking to martyrdom. Hence blessed Cyprian says: "The first title of victory is to confess the Lord when seized by the hands of the gentiles; the second step to glory is to be withdrawn by a cautious retreat and kept for the Lord. The former is a public confession, the latter a private one. The one conquers the judge of this world; the other, content with God as his judge, preserves the integrity of his heart with a pure conscience." This is also most clearly proved from the two sons of Zebedee, in that James, killed by Herod, is said [to have been] given to martyrdom by public confession.
passages.notes: "perseculionis" read as "persecutionis"; "judicc" as "judice". The final word "do." is split across the boundary ("do-dicatur", i.e. "dedicated/given over"), completed from the following context.
